what_happened: The job to add two defaults (version pins and explicit check-tool paths) to defaults.toml was rejected. The verifier found 3 of 6 acceptance criteria unmet. (1) The form/scope criterion: entries must match the other entries and existing entries must keep their meaning. (2) The criterion for a new test that renders the reader's default context and asserts both new ids and key phrases. (3) The criterion that existing defaults tests and the reader's 2,000-token budget test pass, with the new statements terse and wordy ones tightened without dropping content. Three blocker/major findings: to fit the budget (3 tokens of headroom) the job split five existing defaults (buy-first, tested, public, verified, lazy-requests) so the reader's first-sentence render lost their rules; the reader's rendered context lacks the bump-command and silent-fallback halves of the new policies, so the reader can still ask those questions; and the reading did not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met. No failed checks are listed.
cause: Nothing ties a defaults addition to the reader's budget or to how defaults are rendered. The reading did not state that only 3 tokens of headroom remained, nor that the render shows only the first sentence of each entry. It also accepted a criterion allowing existing statements to be tightened "without dropping content", which the planned test could not check. So the producer had to choose between overflowing the budget, dropping policy halves, or cutting existing rules, and no early check compared the reading with the request or the render. Only the final verifier saw the damage. A reading that misstated the request let passing criteria prove little.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before the producer is dispatched and again before verification. It would render each role's default context from the real defaults.toml and report the remaining token room. It would also assert that every existing default's rendered text is unchanged, unless the reading names it as edited, and that each new entry's required phrases appear in the render. A reading that adds defaults must either fit the reported headroom or list a budget raise as a deliverable.
proposed_request: Add two defaults to defaults.toml for the reader: (1) pinned-versions: tool and runtime versions are pinned exactly in config, and a version bump is made only through the bump command, never by letting the tool float; (2) explicit-tool-paths: check tools are run from configured explicit paths, and a missing path is an error, never a silent fallback to another tool. Each entry needs applies_to and a source citing this request, in the same form as the other entries. First measure the reader set's remaining token room in the rendered context. Both new entries must show their full rule, including the bump command and the no-silent-fallback halves, in the first sentence that the render shows. If they do not fit within the 2,000-token budget, raise the reader set's budget by the smallest amount needed and say so in the changelog. Do not split, shorten or drop any existing default's rule. Add a test that builds the reader's default context from the real defaults.toml (defaults().render()) and asserts it contains both new ids and the key phrases of both halves of each, plus a test that every existing default's rendered text is unchanged. Only defaults.toml, the budget setting if a raise is needed, one test file and CHANGELOG.md may change. cargo test must pass, including every_role_set_is_within_its_budget.
